statement: A dissolved Delaware corporation (or successor entity) that has not followed the elective § 280 notice procedure must, before the § 278 three-year continuation period expires, adopt a plan of distribution that pays or makes reasonable provision for known claims and obligations (including contingent and unmatured contractual claims), for compensation in pending actions, and for claims likely to arise or become known within 10 years after dissolution, before distributing remaining assets to stockholders (8 Del. C. § 281(b)).
caveat: The elective path (§§ 280, 281(a)) runs a notice-based claims process with different protections for directors and stockholders; this rule states only the default § 281(b) duty. Claim priorities and the sufficiency of a provision are fact-specific. This repo does not draft or adopt a plan of distribution.
